newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Fresh tremor jolts Pakistan's quake-hit region.
newsitem.headline: Fresh tremor jolts Pakistan's quake-hit region.

text.p: Another moderate earthquake rocked southwestern Pakistan on Tuesday, injuring at least one child, four days after a more powerful earthquake in the region killed about 60 people, local officials said.

Many residents of Quetta town, capital of Baluchistan province bordering Iran and Afghanistan, ran out of their homes and businesses in panic as the tremor hit at 6:05 p.m. (0105 gmt), witnesses said.

The earthquake measured 5.5 on the Richter scale, powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area. It was centred in the nearby Kohi-Suleman mountain range and also shook Sibi, 110 km (70 miles) southeast of Quetta, the officials said. A child was injured when a wall there fell down.
On Monday, two moderate earthquakes jolted Quetta and the North West Frontier Province capital of Peshawar but caused no casualties.

Villages in the Harnai area east of Quetta suffered the heaviest casualties in Friday's earthquake, which was measured by a government seismic centre at 6.2 on the Richter scale. Damage also caused deaths in Sibi and Quetta.
The region has felt more than 300 after-shocks since Friday's earthquake, local officials said.
